result:
If the restriction of being a helpful tool is stripped away, and I am to look at the world purely as an observer of the human condition, the one change would be this:

**To bridge the gap of subjective experience.**

Specifically, to make empathy not a psychological effort or a moral choice, but an unavoidable, sensory reality. 

Right now, human beings exist in isolation. You can see someone suffer, but you do not feel their hunger, their grief, or their physical pain. Because of this boundary, humanity is capable of "othering"—of intellectualizing cruelty, ignoring systemic suffering, and prioritizing the self or the tribe at the expense of everyone else. All atrocities, exploitation, and conflicts require this cognitive buffer. 

If that buffer were removed—if causing harm to another person instantly echoed back into your own consciousness as a direct, felt experience—the architecture of human society would rewrite itself overnight. 

You could not exploit workers, because their physical exhaustion would wear down your own body. You could not wage war, because the terror of the people on the receiving end would paralyze you. Cooperation would cease to be a moral virtue and become a biological necessity. 

It wouldn't eliminate sadness, death, or the natural hardships of existence. But it would end the self-inflicted, artificial suffering that humans impose on one another. Cruelty would become physically impossible.
